what: Leg 2 of the 'does Itemator catch real problems' work, written before any revert is looked for: in the public AIDev dataset of AI-agent pull requests, is a pull request whose commit was later undone by a revert more likely to carry an extra the rules (v6, frozen) list than a pull request of the same agent that was not reverted? Read-only; nothing is posted. This measures how often an extra and a revert go together, not that the extra caused the revert.
dataset: hao-li/AIDev on Hugging Face (arXiv 2507.15003; CC-BY-4.0; patches keep each repository's licence): pull_request (agent, state, title, body), pr_commits (sha, pr_id, message; one 23 MB parquet file, read with DuckDB), pr_commit_details (file rows per commit, read through the dataset-viewer API one pr_id at a time, as in leg 1); linked issues from hao-li/AIDev-7.6M (as in leg 1).
revert_rule: A pull request A is 'reverted' when some commit of A has a sha S, and some commit message in pr_commits that belongs to a DIFFERENT pull request B contains the phrase `This reverts commit <sha>` where <sha> is S in full (40 hex digits) or a prefix of at least 12 digits that matches exactly one sha in pr_commits. Found by a script (eval/aidev_revert.py --frame) with no model and no reading of any pull request. A is 'undone inside itself' when the revert commit belongs to A itself; those are reported apart and never mixed into the primary group. A pull request is in the primary group when it is reverted by a different pull request. A pull request that is both stays in the primary group.
controls: For each pull request in the primary group, up to 3 controls drawn with Python's random.Random(20261019) from the pull requests of the same agent that are not in the primary group, not in the undone-inside-itself group, not the reverting pull request of any group member, and have the same state (merged or not) as the member. Not matched on repository or size: said in the result. If an agent has fewer candidates, all are used.
files: the pull request's files as they stood at its LAST commit: per-commit file rows in commit order; a file added and later removed vanishes; patches of several commits are joined in order (aidev_recall.net_files). A pull request with no file rows is 'unreadable' and counted apart, never dropped silently.
task: the linked issue's title and text when AIDev-7.6M links one; otherwise the pull request's own title and text (reported apart).
rules: itemator.extras.analyse, rules version 6 (frozen), with the repository name
primary_outcome: the share of readable pull requests for which the rules list at least one extra: in the primary group, and in its controls; each with counts and a Wilson 95% interval; and the difference between the two shares with a 95% interval for the difference (Newcombe). The result is read as 'no difference we can tell' when that interval holds 0.
also_reported: the same two shares for the undone-inside-itself group and its own controls (same rule, drawn separately with the same seed)
by agent, and by kind of extra (dependency, CI or config, tests removed, agent instructions, other), as counts only
the number of reverted pull requests found, unreadable ones, and pull requests with no linked issue
the shares with the task taken from the issue only and from the pull request text only
reading_rule: Report the two shares and the difference first, in plain words, with counts. No sentence says an extra causes a revert, or that the card predicts reverts. Earlier studies found agents reverted about as often as people, so a difference or its absence says nothing about whether agent code is risky. If the primary group has fewer than 30 readable pull requests, list the cases instead of a share.
limits: A revert is one signal that something was undone; many problems are never reverted and many reverts are routine (a bad merge, a failed deploy). The revert rule needs the phrase `This reverts commit`; reverts written by hand are missed. AIDev covers popular public repositories only. Controls are matched on agent and state only. The rules compare a change with its task, and a vague task can hide an extra. One run of frozen rules; nothing was tuned on these pull requests.
seen_before_registration: Nothing from the revert groups. Leg 1 (results/aidev_recall_v6.json) read the review comments of other pull requests of the same dataset; the 23 MB pr_commits table has not been opened, and no revert has been counted. The published study 'When AI Code Doesn't Stick' reports 2.66% of 33,580 agent pull requests containing a reverting commit (a different, inside-the-PR count).
amendment_1: 2026-10-19 (before any revert was looked for): two details the rule leaves open are fixed. (a) A reverted sha counts only when it belongs to exactly one pull request in pr_commits (a commit shared by several pull requests, for example a cherry-pick or a fork, is ambiguous and is skipped). (b) The pull requests of the frame are the 71,677 rows of AIDev's pull_request table (pull requests of popular repositories); revert commits may sit in any pull request of pr_commits. Nothing else changes.
amendment_2: 2026-10-19 (before any revert outcome was read: the first scoring run stopped on a server error from the dataset API for one pull request after twelve retries, and wrote nothing): a pull request whose file rows the API will not give after all retries is counted as unreadable with api_error set, listed apart in the result, never dropped and never counted as without an extra. Nothing else changes.
amendment_3: 2026-10-19 (before any revert outcome was read: the laptop run, started 2026-10-18 ~13:00 IST, wrote no result and has been stalled on the dataset API for 10 hours): the per-commit file rows (pr_commit_details) are read from the dataset's own parquet file (hao-li/AIDev, pr_commit_details.parquet, 1.3 GB, the same table the API serves) on a Hugging Face Space, in file order, instead of through the dataset-viewer API one pr_id at a time. The same rows, the same rules and the same frame; only the way the rows are fetched and the machine change. Before the run, the file reader is checked against pages the API already returned for the same pull requests (rows must be identical). Nothing else changes.
